evidence.excerpt: Two standard seal-quality tests—the 180° peel test and the differential pressure burst test—were applied to heat-sealed pouches made from OPP/tie/mLLDPE films sealed across a jaw temperature range of 95–140 °C. For each jaw temperature, 20 pouches were prepared and tested by both methods. Peel force data and burst pressure data were analysed for correlation and for their ability to discriminate between adequate and inadequate seals. The two methods agreed in classifying seals above 110 °C as acceptable (peel ≥ 25 N/25 mm; burst ≥ 180 kPa), but diverged in the 100–109 °C zone, where 7 of 20 pouches passed the burst test but failed the peel criterion. Root-cause analysis by SEM cross-section showed incomplete interdiffusion at the seal interface in those pouches. Repeatability expressed as coefficient of variation was 5.8 % for peel and 9.2 % for burst across all jaw temperatures. The peel test is recommended as the more conservative acceptance criterion for VFFS applications handling liquid or particulate products.
